Later Adulthood 
As the body ages, muscle mass progressively declines. This breakdown of skeletal muscle mass is known as 
sarcopenia (Azzolino et al., 2021). The strength and functionality of the muscles begin to decline as well (Figure 
20.3). Bone mass and density also begin to diminish, which can lead to increased risk for fractures and decreased 
mobility (Azzolini, 2021). For older adults with sarcopenia, dietary interventions are effective for building muscle 
mass. Table 20.7 highlights some effective ways the older adult with sarcopenia can increase muscle mass.

Manage chronic conditions. 
Many chronic conditions can lead to a sedentary lifestyle, which, in turn, 
can lead to muscle loss. By managing these conditions, the older adult 
may be able to become more active.
